title: Graceful cross-region takeover with predictive cache warmup and composite health score
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During unplanned regional outages we need the target region to assume traffic without noticeable latency spikes or model degradation. Current warm-standby behavior is reactive: when traffic is re-routed we often observe cold KV-cache misses, increased model disk reads for sharded weights, and a transient SLO breach window.

Goal: Implement a takeover coordinator and readiness scoring system that performs predictive warmup (based on recent traffic and synthetic trace replay), validates a composite readiness score across runtime subsystems (KV cache, kernel residency, GPU availability, version compatibility), and gates automated failover until safety thresholds are met. The system must also support fast, staged cutovers when manual override is required.

Scope: Orchestration and readiness checks for Redwood Private/Dedicated and Hosted regions. Work includes: 1) predictive trace generation service for cache prewarming, 2) readiness scoring service that aggregates signals and produces an accept/reject decision, 3) integration into smart routing controller with staged cutover and rollback, 4) observability and runbooks for on-call and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive warmup can replay a 5-minute synthetic trace based on last-10min traffic profile and achieve >= 65% KV cache hit rate within 90s on target pool for 90% of trials
Readiness score composed from KV hit rate, half-life of key evictions, model-shard residency (on-GPU fraction), and local health probes. Failover only allowed if score >= 0.7 and no critical errors
Orchestrator supports automatic staged cutover: shadowing traffic (100% shadow for 5m), 5% live canary, 25% ramp, then 100% within preconfigured windows and rollback on threshold breach
Controller emits detailed events to EventLog, exposes per-region readiness metric, and integrates with Console rollouts dashboard
SRE runbook and automated rollback playbook added to Runbooks repo with clear thresholds and escalation steps
plan: Design phase: finalize readiness score composition and thresholds with SRE and runtime teams (week 1)
Implement predictive trace generator service and replay harness (week 2-3)
Expose runtime probes for KV cache hit rate, eviction half-life, model shard residency, kernel warm % (week 3)
Build readiness aggregator and decision API with audit log entries (week 4)
Integrate with smart-routing controller for staged cutovers and shadowing (week 5)
End-to-end testing in staging with induced failure drills and chaos experiments (week 6)
Ship to canary regions then full rollout; publish runbook and dashboard tiles (week 7)
risks: Predictive replay could overload target pool if profiles are inaccurate — need conservative throttles and dry-run mode
False positives in readiness score could keep traffic in failing region — include quorum of independent probes
Model variant compatibility issues during fallback — must verify model hash compatibility and automatic variant mapping
Telemetry gaps leading to opaque failures — require new traces and tracing hooks before gating rollout
tests: Staging chaos test: simulate regional controller failure and validate orchestrated takeover completes without SLO violation in >= 9/10 runs
Load test: synthetic trace replays at 2x normal load to verify throttles and no resource exhaustion
Canary rollback test: intentionally trigger degraded readiness mid-ramp and verify automated rollback within configured window
Integration test: model-variant fallback exercised while maintaining deterministic output parity for sampled prompts
observability: Add Console tile: Region Readiness, with score breakdown and trendline
EventLog entries for each stage of orchestrator (warmup_start, warmup_complete, shadow_start, canary_start, ramp_complete, rollback)
Trace span tags to link synthetic replay to readiness decisions
Alerting: fire when readiness_score < 0.5 for target region during automated cutover
